action: If you bought tickets on Fandango recently, check your card statements for charges you do not recognise, ask your bank for a replacement card if you receive a notice, and follow the steps in Fandango's notification.
exec: Card data was captured at checkout on a major ticketing site, creating fraud exposure for customers and liability for the company.
plain: Ticket seller Fandango is telling customers that payment card details typed into its checkout pages were exposed in a breach. The number of people affected is not yet known.
summary: Fandango is notifying customers that card-skimming code injected into its checkout page captured payment details entered between October 8 and 11, 2026, according to BleepingComputer's report of the notice. Exposed data: card number, CVV, expiry, billing ZIP and email; names, ID and SSNs were not. Fandango says it determined on October 30 that data may be affected and knows of no fraud. The number affected was not disclosed.
title: Fandango says hackers stole payment card details from checkout pages

validation.note: BleepingComputer article read in full (Nov 16); Fandango's own notice (DocumentCloud copy) not opened.

review.note: BleepingComputer read in full: summary lacked facts; now states skimmer on checkout page, Oct 8-11 exposure, data types, Oct 30 determination, no count disclosed
